title: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
name: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
metaTitle: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing in Oklahoma City, OK
metaDescription: Triple net and single-tenant net lease replacement property sourcing in Oklahoma City, checked corridor by corridor against your 1031 basis and hold period.

sections.html: A single-tenant net lease deal reads simple on a one-page summary, one tenant, one roof, one rent check, but the diligence underneath it is where exchanges get delayed. Oklahoma City's net lease inventory runs along the I-35 and I-40 corridors, at retail pads feeding off energy-sector office traffic, and out toward the growth ring in Yukon and Mustang. We source triple net and single-tenant net lease replacement property against your basis and your tolerance for landlord responsibilities that don't show up in the lease summary.

sections.heading: Corridor by Corridor: Where OKC's Net Lease Stock Sits
sections.html:
Interchange pad sites along I-35 and I-40 carry the deepest tenant pool, since national operators chase the same traffic counts and are willing to sign longer terms for that visibility. The Memorial Road corridor holds a mix of pad sites and small strip parcels, while the growth ring in Yukon and Mustang keeps adding new construction as rooftops push west of the metro core.

Downtown, Bricktown's net lease retail rides the foot traffic that MAPS-driven redevelopment has brought into the urban core, which is a different tenant profile than a highway pad site built purely for drive-through volume. We match corridor to tenant type before we match tenant type to price, since the wrong pairing shows up as vacancy risk years later.

sections.heading: Lease Structure Details That Change Who's Responsible for What
sections.html:
Two net lease deals with identical rent can carry completely different landlord obligations, so we check the actual lease language before a property goes on your list:

  • Whether roof and structure responsibility sits with the landlord or the tenant
  • HVAC replacement responsibility and any capped landlord contribution
  • Common area maintenance reconciliation history and any disputed charges
  • Percentage rent triggers, if any, and how they're reported
  • Co-tenancy or exclusive-use clauses tied to a specific corridor location
  • Remaining primary lease term against your intended hold period

We put these findings in writing before recommending a property, since a landlord-responsible roof on an older building changes the real economics of the deal.

sections.heading: Reading Tenant Credit the Way You'd Read a Service Vendor
sections.html:
A brand name on the sign isn't the same as a strong tenant, so we look at operating history at that specific Oklahoma City location, comparing sales performance where available against comparable stores in the same operator's portfolio. A franchisee-operated store carries different risk than a corporate-guaranteed lease, and we flag which one you're actually buying before you commit basis to it.

We also watch for dark-store risk, where a tenant closes the physical location but keeps paying rent through the lease term. That preserves your cash flow on paper but eliminates the co-tenancy value that neighboring tenants were counting on, and it can make the property harder to re-lease if that tenant eventually walks away entirely.

sections.heading: Matching Net Lease Term to Your Exchange Timeline
sections.html: Remaining lease term matters as much as rent when you're matching a replacement property to your hold period, and we flag any absolute net or ground lease structure separately from a standard triple net deal since the landlord obligations differ. Any seller concessions, credits, or security deposit transfers get routed through your qualified intermediary correctly rather than handled outside escrow, which protects the exchange from a constructive receipt problem down the line.

sections.heading: Sourcing Against the 45-Day Clock in a Thin Market
sections.html: Net lease inventory in Oklahoma City is competitive right now partly because out-of-state exchange buyers are drawn to the no-coastal-pricing value play here, so we plan overlapping candidates on your identification list rather than a single target. If your replacement property carries less debt than your relinquished property, talk to your tax advisor about boot exposure before you lock the deal, since debt replacement matters as much as price to how the exchange gets treated.

faqs.q: What's the practical difference between NNN and STNL for exchange purposes?
faqs.a: Both terms describe a single-tenant net lease structure where the tenant covers most operating costs, and either can qualify as like-kind replacement real estate. The practical difference is in the specific lease terms, so we compare the actual landlord obligations rather than relying on the label a broker used in the marketing package.

faqs.q: Does a franchisee-operated location carry more risk than a corporate-guaranteed lease?
faqs.a: Generally yes, since a corporate guarantee gives you a stronger credit backstop if the franchisee entity struggles. We flag which structure applies to a given property before it goes on your identification list so you're underwriting the actual guarantor rather than assuming the brand name carries the lease.

faqs.q: What happens if the tenant closes the store but keeps paying rent?
faqs.a: Rent continues, but co-tenancy value for the center and foot traffic for neighboring tenants can decline. We flag any dark-store history at a property during sourcing since it changes the long-term outlook even when current cash flow looks stable, and it can complicate re-leasing if that tenant eventually exits the lease altogether.

faqs.q: How do I avoid taking on boot if the replacement property carries less debt than the relinquished one?
faqs.a: You generally need to match or exceed both the value and the debt on your relinquished property, or bring additional cash to offset a debt reduction. This is a tax question specific to your situation, so confirm the exact treatment with your tax advisor or qualified intermediary before closing rather than assuming a rule of thumb applies.

faqs.q: Why is Oklahoma City net lease inventory hard to find in a 45-day window?
faqs.a: Demand from out-of-state exchange buyers targeting non-coastal pricing keeps good net lease product moving quickly, so we start sourcing candidates before your relinquished property even closes to make sure you have real options once the clock starts, rather than scrambling once the identification deadline is already running.
